classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the factors as two orders of selecting all hires and their higher-responsibility subset, adjusting the remaining pool and required hires.

content.prompt:
A group of $n$ candidates apply for $r$ job openings, which includes $k$ positions of higher responsibility. By considering the number of ways to fill the open positions and positions of higher responsibility, show that
$$\binom{n}{r}\binom{r}{k}=\binom{n}{k}\binom{n-k}{r-k}.$$

answer.short:
$\binom{n}{r}\binom{r}{k}=\binom{n}{k}\binom{n-k}{r-k}$.

Choose all hires before the higher-responsibility subset, or choose that subset before the remaining hires.
answer.worked:
Choose the $r$ successful candidates in $\binom{n}{r}$ ways, then choose $k$ of them for higher responsibility in $\binom{r}{k}$ ways. This gives $\binom{n}{r}\binom{r}{k}$ outcomes.

Alternatively, choose the $k$ higher-responsibility candidates first in $\binom{n}{k}$ ways. Choose the remaining $r-k$ hires from the other $n-k$ candidates in $\binom{n-k}{r-k}$ ways.

Both methods count the same hired team with the same higher-responsibility subset, so
$$\binom{n}{r}\binom{r}{k}=\binom{n}{k}\binom{n-k}{r-k}.$$
